other_failure_modes.name: Feature engineering leakage within cross-validation
other_failure_modes.description: Stateful feature engineering transformations (like TF-IDF, SVD, frequency encoding, and group-by aggregations) are fitted on the entire training set before the cross-validation loop. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the CV scores overly optimistic.

other_failure_modes.name: Brittle train-test feature alignment
other_failure_modes.description: Conditional logic applied independently to the train and test sets can result in mismatched columns. If a feature meets a condition (e.g., minimum value >= 0) in the train set but not in the test set, the resulting dataframes will have different columns, leading to runtime errors when aligning them.

summary: The agent provides a robust, well-structured solution with cross-validation, multiple gradient boosting models, and an optimized ensemble. However, there is data leakage within the cross-validation loop where stateful features (TF-IDF, SVD, and aggregations) are fitted on the entire training set before splitting. Additionally, a logic flaw in feature extraction could cause runtime errors if test set distributions differ slightly from the training set.
